UDO Proposed Amendments #2010-2 Brian Temerson, applicant A proposal to amend Section 4.4.8 of the Lincoln County Unified Development Ordinance to revise the standards for gas stations/convenience stores and accessory automatic car washes and to amend Section 3.2.6 to allow service bay doors of accessory automatic car washes to face the road without being screened.

Planning Board voted 9-0 to recommend disapproval, with the exception of recommending in favor of amending Section 4.4.8.C.2 to change the maximum building dimensions of a one-bay automatic car wash to 30 x 65 feet.

CZ #2010-4 Tawnya Cagley, applicant (Parcel ID# 18472) A request to rezone 1.5 acres from B- N (Neighborhood Business) to CZ B-G (Conditional Zoning General Business) to permit a car sales lot. The property is located at 2037 W. Hwy. 150, on the south side of Hwy. 150 about 1,200 feet east of Old Lincolnton-Crouse Road, in Lincolnton Township.
Planning Board voted 9-0 to recommend approval.

CUP #299 Cindy Kincaid, applicant (Parcel ID# 10425) A request for a conditional use permit to operate a riding stable and hold horse shows in the R-R (Rural Residential) district. The 20-acre parcel is located at 3377 Flay Sain Road, on the east side of Flay Sain Road abut 300 feet north of the Gaston County line, in North Brook Township.
Planning Board voted 9-0 to table request.
Adopted by the Lincoln County Planning Board on November 1, 2010

These proposed amendments are inconsistent with the Lincoln County Comprehensive Land Use Plan and other adopted plans in that:
The Land Use Plans calls for applying additional standards to nonresidential development, including standards for building orientation.
These proposed amendments are not reasonable and not in the public interest in that:

These standards were adopted to enhance the appearance of gas stations/convenience stores, to protect residential properties from the close proximity of structures associated with gas stations/convenience stores, and to guard against potential traffic problems from vehicles exiting automatic car washes at main parking areas and driveways.
The first part of No. 4 of the proposed amendments is reasonable and is in the public interest in that it deals only with size of a one-bay automatic car wash.
Adopted by the Lincoln County Planning Board on November 1, 2010
This proposed amendment is inconsistent with the Lincoln County Comprehensive Land Use Plan and other adopted plans in that:
The Land Use Plan classifies this area as residential.
This proposed amendment is reasonable and in the public interest in that:

The proposed use is compatible with this area. Most of the properties on this side of Hwy. 150 in this area are zoned business or industrial. This property is located between two vehicle service garages. This is a well-established business area that is separated from residential areas by a highway and a railroad.

The Lincoln County Public Library will be conducting a 3-day “FOOD FOR FINES” drive Thanksgiving week. Monday, November 22nd thru Wednesday, November 24th, patrons may bring in canned or non-perishable food items as “payment” for library fines. Up to $5.00 can be waived per account at the rate of $1.00 per donated food item. Donations received at Lincoln County Library sites will be used for the BackPack Program which sends nutritious food home to assist Lincoln County school children. The library hopes its patrons will take advantage of this opportunity to reduce the amount of fines they owe while helping out needy families in our own community.
Believe it or not, there are children in Lincoln County that do not have adequate food over the weekend. We need your help to feed these hungry children at our local schools through the weekends.
The food should be non-perishable, microwavable, with a long expiration date. Individual portions preferred. No glass jars or expired food, please.
